before.heading: Explain the award's price consequences before entry.
before.intro: An award that purchases a work differs from an award added to its sale price. Keep the selected award's entry requirements, accepted-price restrictions and later artwork delivery stages connected.
before.customerQuestion: Does this award buy my work or add to its sale, and which conditions follow from choosing it?

decisions.label: Describe the award relationship precisely
decisions.body: Use the current call's exact wording to distinguish a purchase amount from an additional award. Keep any minimum-entry requirement attached only to the applicable award. Do not calculate a net payment where commission or award treatment remains ambiguous; obtain the organization's explanation.

decisions.label: Separate entry from accepted-work handling
decisions.body: Explain when prices become fixed and identify the instructions that apply after acceptance. Entry-mail and physical-artwork addresses may differ. Carry approved carrier, return and pickup requirements with the artwork stage so an artist does not reuse entry instructions for shipment.

decisions.label: Keep each annual call accurately dated
decisions.body: Mark concluded calls closed and retain useful past results under their year. A new call needs approved dates, award terms and submission instructions. Agree which details require annual review so a reused layout does not silently carry forward old deadlines or conditions.

ownerInputs: Current approved prospectus, exact award terms and entry requirements.
Accepted-price and commission explanations, with ambiguities resolved.
Current dates, separate entry/artwork addresses, carrier and return instructions.
before.sourceBridge: The concluded 2026 Bosque Arts Center Art Classic is a historical example: the John Steven Jones Purchase Award buys one piece for its stated amount regardless of listed price, while an Art Patrons award adds to a sale. The prospectus also distinguishes award-entry requirements and artwork delivery.
before.limits: The 2026 event is not an open submission opportunity. The organization approves current financial and shipping terms. Secure submissions, file uploads and payments require separate assessment.

decisions.label: Separate entry from accepted-work handling
decisions.body: Explain when prices become fixed and identify the instructions that apply after acceptance. Entry-mail and physical-artwork addresses may differ. Label each address by its purpose so an artist does not reuse an entry destination for shipment of an accepted piece.

decisions.label: Plan the artwork’s return or pickup
decisions.body: Keep the organization’s approved carrier, return and pickup instructions with the accepted-work stage. A fictional artist question could ask, “If my accepted piece is not sold, which return or pickup arrangement must I prepare?” Staff should resolve that plan using the applicable prospectus. The question does not invent prepaid shipping, a carrier commitment or a collection deadline.

requiredFixes: Keep annual archive/update and handoff commitments in the FAQ. Use decision three for the artist’s accepted-work return or pickup stage, based on approved carrier and return instructions, while retaining the historical-event disclosure.

limits: Draft only. Historical disclosure and annual-call FAQ preserved. No current financial, carrier, deadline or event terms invented.

acceptance.scope: Content only; family, visual, accessibility and release checks remain separate.
